purpose: A research-only thematic radar for Power Stack. It is not a portfolio view. A theme stays active only when recent news, dossier work or the Live Market Deck materially changes the investment mechanism, timing, risk or beneficiaries.

promoteWhen: A material catalyst changes the mechanism or timing of a thesis
At least two research streams converge, such as market news plus dossier or Live Market Deck evidence
The theme has a clear next test that can strengthen or invalidate it
parkWhen: The thesis remains structurally valid but nothing material has changed
The theme duplicates a broader active mechanism
The signal is mostly valuation excitement without improving commercial evidence

themes.name: Long-End Yield Stress / Duration Compression
themes.status: Active macro regime / high cross-asset impact
themes.summary: Long-duration assets are being constrained by the long end of the Treasury curve even without a matching hawkish shift in near-term Fed pricing. Oil-driven inflation risk, heavy sovereign borrowing and term-premium concerns are keeping 10- to 30-year yields high enough to compress valuations across AI, grid, robotics and other capital-intensive growth themes.
themes.whyDeveloping: Treasury's larger long-end buybacks produced only temporary relief. By August 21, the U.S. 10-year yield was back around 4.7% and the 30-year near 5.24%-5.25%, while global equities were heading for their weakest week since mid-July. The useful question has shifted from 'will the Fed hike?' to 'how expensive is duration when fiscal and energy risk keep the long end elevated?'

mainNews.title: Bond yields and oil keep pressure on global equities after buyback relief fades
mainNews.implication: The valuation regime for capital-intensive growth is increasingly set by long-end funding costs rather than the next Fed meeting alone.

themes.name: AI Buildout: Power, Grid + Cooling Bottlenecks
themes.summary: AI demand is still strong, but the scarce inputs are increasingly outside the GPU: generation, transmission, substations, switchgear, interconnection, cooling and water. The best evidence is moving from hyperscaler capex announcements toward actual equipment demand, lead times and site constraints.
themes.whyDeveloping: Texas now requires more explicit scrutiny of grid dependence, on-site power, water and cooling for large data-centre projects, while Rockwell Automation is reporting strong semiconductor, data-centre and warehouse-automation demand. That strengthens the case that enabling infrastructure can monetise before more speculative AI applications.

mainNews.title: Texas data-centre review broadens the bottleneck from electricity to full-site infrastructure
mainNews.source: Office of the Governor of Texas / PUCT-ERCOT directive
mainNews.implication: Projects without credible power, water and cooling plans face higher execution risk; scarce enabling equipment gains strategic value.

mainNews.title: Rockwell reports 10% organic growth with strength in semiconductor, data centre and warehouse automation
mainNews.implication: Real industrial demand is confirming that the physical layer of AI and automation is already commercialising.

themes.name: AI Buildout: Financing + Cash Conversion
themes.summary: The AI capex debate is shifting from demand to funding quality. As infrastructure providers spend billions before cash flows arrive, debt capacity, convertibles, dilution, utilisation and contracted returns become as important as revenue growth.
themes.whyDeveloping: Nebius upsized its latest convertible offering to $5 billion, potentially $5.75 billion, after spending about $5.7 billion on Q2 capex despite a quarterly loss. Demand is not the immediate problem; the market is now testing how efficiently that demand can be financed without destroying per-share economics.

mainNews.title: Nebius upsizes convertible financing to $5 billion as data-centre buildout accelerates
mainNews.implication: Strong capital demand confirms the buildout, but financing quality and dilution are becoming the main discriminator between AI infrastructure winners.

themes.name: Middle Distillates > Gasoline: Product Split
themes.direction: diesel and jet remain extreme; gasoline starting to ease
themes.summary: The refined-product shortage is splitting internally. Washington can add gasoline supply relatively quickly by relaxing blending rules, but it cannot manufacture diesel and jet-fuel refining capacity nearly as fast. The useful hierarchy is increasingly diesel/jet >> gasoline >> crude rather than treating the 3-2-1 as one uniform signal.
themes.whyDeveloping: The EPA authorised an early September 1 switch to winter-grade gasoline, potentially adding hundreds of thousands of barrels per day of gasoline supply. That arrives as gasoline cracks soften while the U.S. diesel crack remains around the unprecedented $100-per-barrel area. A falling headline 3-2-1 could therefore hide a still-severe middle-distillate shortage.
watch: RBOB crack below $50 while ULSD crack remains above $100

mainNews.title: US ends summer-blend gasoline requirement early to increase supply
mainNews.implication: Policy may compress RBOB and the headline 3-2-1 without resolving the harder diesel/jet refining-capacity shortage.

mainNews.title: U.S. diesel crack surpasses $100 per barrel for the first time
mainNews.implication: The global replacement barrel for middle distillates remains scarce even with U.S. refineries running hard.

mainNews.title: Iran-war energy stress is increasingly a refining-capacity problem
mainNews.implication: Damaged processing capacity and depleted inventories can keep industrial-fuel inflation elevated after crude stops accelerating.

themes.name: Fertilizer: Nitrogen Advantage vs Sulphur Constraint
themes.status: New resource-scarcity theme / high agriculture relevance
themes.summary: Fertilizer is not one trade. Global nitrogen remains constrained by Gulf outages and trade disruption while U.S. natural gas stays comparatively cheap, creating a potential margin advantage for North American nitrogen producers. Phosphate faces the opposite problem: scarce sulphur is raising input costs so aggressively that high fertilizer prices can coexist with producer curtailments and weak margins.
themes.whyDeveloping: CF Industries estimates the Iran conflict removed roughly 4.0-4.5 million tonnes of traded Middle East urea and about 1 million tonnes of ammonia, while the Power Stack macro dashboard still shows Henry Hub around $2.8. At the same time, nearly half of seaborne sulphur normally moves through Hormuz and Mosaic has curtailed phosphate production because spot sulphur economics are unsustainable. This is an unusually clean example of the bottleneck sitting one layer below the headline commodity.

mainNews.title: Iran-war fertilizer disruption exposes food-production vulnerability
mainNews.implication: High fertilizer costs can reduce planting and application, turning an input shortage into a later crop-yield problem.

mainNews.title: CF Industries says global nitrogen supply remains constructive into 2027
mainNews.implication: Cheap North American gas plus globally supported nitrogen pricing creates a differentiated producer setup rather than generic fertilizer beta.

mainNews.title: Mosaic reduces phosphate operations in Brazil because of sulphur constraints
mainNews.implication: High phosphate prices do not guarantee producer margins when the scarce input is sulphur.

themes.name: Water Scarcity: Food + Power + Freight Collision
themes.summary: Water scarcity is broadening beyond data-centre cooling. The same drought is reducing crop yields, constraining river freight and forcing nuclear/hydro generation cuts, making leak reduction, reuse, distribution efficiency and resilient water infrastructure more economically valuable.
themes.whyDeveloping: Europe's August drought has pushed major rivers toward historic lows, cut French maize expectations sharply and forced nuclear output reductions across the Danube region. Yet irrigation-equipment sales remain weak because farm economics are poor, creating an important investment split between municipally financed water infrastructure and farmer-funded equipment.

mainNews.title: Europe's deepening drought hits water, crops, shipping and power
mainNews.implication: Water is becoming a multi-sector operating constraint rather than a standalone environmental theme.

mainNews.title: French drought threatens severe maize losses and deeper EU crop shortfall
mainNews.implication: Water scarcity is beginning to transmit directly into crop supply and import requirements.

mainNews.title: Mueller Water Products raises EBITDA guidance after strong margin expansion
mainNews.implication: Municipal water-network equipment is already converting infrastructure need into earnings even while residential construction remains soft.

themes.name: Natural Rubber: Acreage + Labour Squeeze
themes.summary: Natural-rubber supply is being eroded by farm economics rather than just weather. Indonesian growers are replacing labour-intensive rubber with more profitable oil palm, creating a slow-moving acreage squeeze that can persist even if tire demand is only moderate.
themes.whyDeveloping: Indonesia's rubber plantation area has fallen about 17% in five years and national output has dropped from above 3 million to roughly 2 million tonnes as growers switch to palm. Sri Trang's Q2 natural-rubber ASP rose to a 12-year high, providing company-level confirmation that supply pressure is reaching realised pricing, although volumes and utilisation remain weak.

mainNews.title: Indonesian rubber growers switch acreage to oil palm
mainNews.implication: Palm and biodiesel economics can structurally remove rubber supply, which is harder to reverse than a temporary weather disruption.

mainNews.title: Sri Trang reports 12-year-high natural-rubber ASP in Q2
mainNews.implication: Realised prices confirm the scarcity signal, but falling YoY volumes and only 50.5% utilisation keep the equity thesis higher-risk.

themes.name: Industrial Automation Before Humanoids
themes.summary: The robotics adoption sequence is becoming clearer: fixed industrial automation and warehouse systems are monetising now, while mobile manipulation and humanoids remain earlier and more valuation-sensitive. The investable edge is shifting toward systems and components with current utilisation rather than headline demonstrations.
themes.whyDeveloping: Rockwell's double-digit organic growth and roughly 30% warehouse-automation industry outlook provide harder commercial evidence than the humanoid capital cycle. Unitree's IPO and World Robot Conference show enormous funding appetite, but useful-work economics and reliability still lag the excitement.

mainNews.title: Rockwell raises growth outlook as warehouse and semiconductor automation strengthen
mainNews.implication: Conventional automation is already converting demand into sales and margins, supporting it as the first stage of the robotics monetisation curve.

mainNews.title: Chinese robot makers push humanoids toward industrial work, but mass adoption remains unproven
mainNews.implication: Humanoids remain a high-upside later stage of the theme, not the base case for near-term robotics earnings.

themes.name: Copper Scarcity, but Squeeze Risk
themes.summary: Copper remains the shared physical input across grids, data centres, electrification and automation, but the recent LME spike mixed genuine scarcity with a positioning squeeze. The structural thesis is intact; the record cash price should not be treated as a clean new earnings baseline.
themes.whyDeveloping: LME cash copper briefly reached about $14,912 per tonne and cash-to-three-month backwardation widened to $545 per tonne as concentrated longs collided with thin available stocks. Warehouse inflows then rapidly eased the squeeze, showing why physical tightness and speculative positioning must be separated.

mainNews.title: LME copper flash squeeze exposes a thin physical buffer
mainNews.implication: Scarcity is real, but the extreme spot price partly reflects positioning; diversified miners remain a more disciplined expression than extrapolating squeeze pricing.

themes.name: Personalized Oncology / mRNA Re-rating
themes.status: New platform signal / high event risk
themes.summary: Healthcare has gained a new high-beta growth narrative after the first positive late-stage result for a personalised mRNA cancer vaccine. The opportunity is larger than one melanoma indication if the platform transfers to other solid tumours, but current valuations are already pricing some of that optionality.
themes.whyDeveloping: Moderna and Merck's Intismeran plus Keytruda reduced melanoma recurrence and spread in a Phase 3 trial, reviving confidence in mRNA outside infectious disease. The next step is not another headline; detailed efficacy, overall-survival, safety, manufacturing and cross-tumour data now determine whether this is a platform or a single-indication win.

mainNews.title: Moderna and Merck report first positive late-stage result for an mRNA cancer vaccine
mainNews.implication: The result can reopen capital and valuation support for personalised oncology, but broader-platform expectations need confirmation from detailed and cross-cancer data.

themes.name: China: Fiscal Infrastructure > Broad Stimulus
themes.direction: strengthening for infrastructure, weak for broad beta
themes.summary: China's policy signal is increasingly selective. With benchmark lending rates left unchanged despite weak domestic data, Beijing is leaning more heavily on fiscal execution and already-funded infrastructure rather than a broad property or consumer reflation.
themes.whyDeveloping: The one-year LPR stayed at 3.00% and the five-year rate at 3.50% for a 15th month, while the finance ministry pledged faster fiscal outlays and bond-funded project execution. That favours power, grid, nuclear and selected industrial infrastructure more than a blanket China cyclical trade.

mainNews.title: China keeps LPRs unchanged for a 15th month despite softer activity
mainNews.implication: The absence of rate cuts reinforces a selective infrastructure-over-broad-reflation reading.

mainNews.title: China pledges faster fiscal support and execution of already-funded projects
mainNews.implication: Fiscal implementation is the near-term policy channel to watch for power, grid, transport and other strategic infrastructure demand.

parkedThemes.reason: Structural thesis remains intact, but there is no fresh fuel-cycle regime change in the latest dossier/live-deck cycle. Water-driven nuclear curtailments are now tracked separately under Water Scarcity: Food + Power + Freight Collision.

parkedThemes.reason: The AI-specific water/cooling thesis remains merged into AI Buildout: Power, Grid + Cooling Bottlenecks. A separate active water card now tracks the new drought-driven food/power/freight collision rather than duplicating data-centre cooling.

parkedThemes.name: Metabolic Health + Obesity
parkedThemes.reason: Still a durable healthcare research category, but recent market-moving healthcare evidence has shifted to personalised oncology.

parkedThemes.reason: The old category was too broad. Its investable pieces are now split into the more specific Fertilizer: Nitrogen Advantage vs Sulphur Constraint and Water Scarcity: Food + Power + Freight Collision themes.

parkedThemes.reason: Reframed as Industrial Automation Before Humanoids to reflect the stronger commercial evidence in fixed and warehouse automation.
